correctness.rationale: The subgroup classification is exhaustive. With kernel \(A=C_r\) and cyclic complement \(B=C_{pq}\), subgroups containing \(A\) are inverse images of subgroups of \(B\), while subgroups disjoint from \(A\) inject into \(B\) and are cyclic of order \(1,p,q,pq\). Fixed-point-freeness gives normalizers \(N_G(P)=N_G(Q)=N_G(B)=B\), so each nonnormal cyclic type has exactly \(r\) conjugates and \(|L_1(G)|=3r+2\). The only permuting partners of a nonnormal cyclic subgroup are \(1,A\) and the three cyclic subgroups in its unique complement, hence exactly five. Summing partner counts over \(L_1(H)\) gives every displayed formula. Independent algebra reproduces the four successive positive differences \(3(r-1)/(2L)\), \(3(r-1)/(4L)\), \(3(r-1)(r-6)/(4(r+2)L)\), and \(12r(r-1)/((r+2)L^2)\); since \(pq\mid r-1\) with distinct primes, \(r\ge7\). The packaged finite semidirect-product checks are corroborative only.

evidence: The 2022 'five relative commutativity degrees' classification uses elementwise relative commutativity, not relative cyclic subgroup commutativity.
